notation.purpose: Condensed moves, replies, and saved positions; never general headings.

motion.name: hint
motion.purpose: Draw the hint arrow from stroke-dashoffset 100 to 0.

motion.name: analysis
motion.purpose: Move the analysis indicator from translateX(0) to translateX(240%).

motion.name: journey-marker
motion.purpose: Show hover and selection on connected journey markers.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation: none !important; transition: none !important; scroll-behavior: auto !important
motion.purpose: Applied to all elements and pseudo-elements when reduced motion is requested.

components.name: Primary button
components.description: The visible next decision: Show hint, Play followed by move notation, or the current practice action.

components.name: Coaching modes
components.description: Three explicit coaching times: before a mistake, after a mistake, or after the game.

components.name: Move choice
components.description: A selectable chess move that controls the board arrow. Phone choices use a 40px minimum height; Play and Why? share the action row below.

components.name: Decision coach
components.description: A compact cue and visible decisions beside the board, or below it on phones. Longer explanations open in a dialog. Completed games with a turning point make Practice this primary. Personal practice keeps answers hidden until help is requested, shows Try again and See the reply for an incorrect move, and distinguishes first-attempt solutions without help from assisted solutions. Next position becomes Finish practice on the last position; completion shows solved and independent counts with one primary Back to game action. Show hint is prominent before help; selected hints show Play with move notation and Why?. Concrete warnings offer Show a move, Play anyway, and Pause warnings. The first engine recommendation is not warned against. Ask Rook is removed; threat checks use the explanation dialog.

components.name: Dialog surface
components.description: A focused surface for secondary tasks, move explanations, threat checks, and full game review. Its header stays visible while content scrolls. Practice selection and saved positions open here; personal practice runs on the main board. Saved rows keep the original move and answer behind What happened? and show independent, assisted, or ready-to-practice status. Game, lesson, report, panel, and selected journey views have revisitable hash URLs; hint URLs retain the exact legal UCI move. Account identifiers and private learning records stay out of URLs.
components.html:
Your game

Practice and saved positions open here.

components.name: Board destinations
components.description: A small board-state sample. In play, the shell fills 100dvh under a 56px header (48px on phones). ResizeObserver fits the board to the width and height left by controls and the guide, capped at 720px. Phones stack the guide below; short landscape windows use two columns. Personal practice uses this same board for up to three distinct saved positions, with progress in the opponent strip and reply controls after an incorrect move. Back to game restores the original game while retaining practice evidence. Refresh reopens the active URL position as practice, with Back to game preserving the saved original game.

components.name: Connected journey
components.description: Six unlocked places connected by dashed paths and selected jade paths. Saved skills and practice attempts establish exploration; distinct saved positions establish tried, solved, and independent counts. A check marks independent evidence. The selected concept offers saved practice or a lesson. Wide maps use two rows and three columns; narrow maps use three rows and two columns; short landscape puts the detail beside the map. Selection has its own hash URL.

narrative.overview:
Nextmove uses a quiet, late-night strategy-game frame. Charcoal surfaces surround warm stone squares, ivory pieces, and jade move marks. The board carries the action; short, plain coaching appears when a decision needs support.

The interface uses code, SVG pieces, and line icons. It has no raster texture or decorative image layer. Type, color, and motion help the player read the next move.
keyCharacteristics: A large, clear board within a quiet charcoal frame.
Jade actions and warm warning states.
DM Sans cues with condensed chess notation.
Small control groups and explanations that open on request.

rules.name: The State Rule
rules.body: Use color to reinforce a visible state, not as its only signal.

rules.name: The Plain Cue Rule
rules.body: Keep coaching in sentence case and plain type. Reserve condensed type for chess notation.

rules.name: The One Screen Rule
rules.body: Keep the board, guide, and main controls visible without page scrolling. Resize the board to fit the available space; do not clip page overflow to hide controls. Pause actions appear once in the guide, with no duplicate sticky action row.

dos: Do keep the board, pieces, destinations, and hint arrow clear at phone size.
Do use jade for actions and current state, with labels or shapes for meaning.
Do keep the coach concise and put longer move explanations and threat checks in dialogs.
Do fit the board, guide, and main controls in one window without page scrolling.
Do preserve keyboard focus, accessible labels, and reduced-motion support.
donts: Don't restore the old olive, acid-yellow, grain, or tilted-mark identity.
Don't add a welcome hero, slogans, or a permanent lesson dashboard to play.
Don't use condensed type for headings or teaching prose.
Don't rely on color alone to explain legal moves, check, or selection.
